claims.text: Conventional automotive exhaust catalysts use Pt nanoparticles on relatively ordered oxide supports and require higher Pt loadings.
A high-entropy spinel oxide containing Cr, Mn, Fe, Co, Ni, Cu, and Zn can be synthesized with high configurational disorder.
The specified high-entropy spinel can serve as a support for dispersed Pt nanoparticles.
Increasing configurational disorder in the spinel support facilitates rapid oxygen-ion mobility.
The disordered support provides a stable Pt-support interface that prevents Pt nanoparticle agglomeration.
Increased configurational disorder promotes oxygen-vacancy formation.
Improved oxygen mobility and oxygen exchange maintain a larger population of catalytically active oxygen sites.
Enhanced oxygen activation by the disordered support improves CO-oxidation activity.
Better Pt nanoparticle dispersion reduces the Pt loading required for catalytic performance.
The high-entropy support inhibits Pt sintering during high-temperature redox cycling.
Pt supported on the disordered high-entropy spinel will have a lower CO-oxidation onset temperature than Pt on a conventional ordered oxide support.
Pt supported on the disordered high-entropy spinel will show superior long-term durability relative to Pt on a conventional ordered oxide support.
The proposed catalyst will reduce Pt consumption while improving activity and durability.
Temperatures of 300°C to 700°C with cyclic redox atmospheres are representative automotive exhaust conditions for evaluating CO oxidation and NOx reduction.
The activity and durability benefits will persist throughout 300°C to 700°C cyclic redox operation.
